Item 11.8: perturb camera metadata (wrong or missing) and remove cues; gait removal is in w2_gait.py.

PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN (2026-10-07, wave 2):
  Cues (all label-free, camera id known before the decision): C1 camera-conditional centering (beta 0.5), C2
  camera-pair prior (lambda 0.1, table from the 92 training identities only), C3 same-camera exclusion (gallery
  tracklets with the query's camera id are ranked last). Baseline: appearance only (cue removed).
  Perturbations of the camera ids that the cue sees (scoring always uses the true ids): 'wrong' = each tracklet's
  camera id is replaced, with probability rho, by a camera id drawn from the empirical camera distribution;
  'missing' = replaced by an UNK token, with probability rho. rho in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}; 8 random draws per
  rho > 0. Timestamps do not exist in the release (see Table avail) and cannot be perturbed.
  Hypotheses and falsification criteria, per encoder and protocol:
   H1 (cue value at rho 0): C1 and C3 raise general mAP over appearance only, identity-cluster paired CI above 0.
      FALSIFIED if a CI includes 0.
   H2 (graceful degradation of C1, C3): at rho = 0.5 the mAP is not more than 1.0 point below the appearance-only
      value (upper CI limit of the difference above -1.0). FALSIFIED if the whole CI lies below -1.0.
   H3 (C3 is fragile): at rho = 1 'wrong', C3 general mAP falls below appearance only, CI below 0. FALSIFIED otherwise.
  Intervals: identity-cluster bootstrap/sign-flip on per-query values averaged over draws; Holm over all mAP tests
  of the run (declared exploratory family).
Outputs results/w2_perturb.json.
usage: python3 -I w2_perturb.py
